### 1. Introduction

#### 1.1. Product Name and Brand

The product is named **Vinyl Superglue** and is backed by the Audi brand, specifically putti (a unique Scandinavian figural style that is popular among Audi vehicles). The logo of Vinyl Superglue is displayed on both the glue bottle caps and the large adhesive labels.

#### 1.2. Product Description

The product is a convenient glue designed for especially urgent and pressing situations. This glue can withstand various stresses up to 4,000 pounds per square inch (PSI), and its tensile strength is over 50,000 PSI. 

#### 1.3. Usage and Application

- **Mechanical Testing:** The glue demonstrated chemical resistance, good adhesion properties, and above-average low expansion and damping properties.
- **Operating Conditions:** The glue performed well under temperatures ranging from -60°C to +200°C.
- **Jigger Tests Dependence:** This product showed high adhesion to various materials, maintaining its strength under various environmental stresses and harsh conditions.

#### 1.4. Features and Benefits

- Increases the bond force, protects against outdoor corrosion, prevents propeller rust, and provides the highest mechanical strength.
- The glue contains a special antioxidant chemical system that can eliminate paint defects and extend the useful life of automotive parts. Reliable effects can be expected after 3 months’ usage.

#### 1.5. Environmental and Safety Assessments

- **RoHS Compliance:** The product is compliant with the Restriction of Hazardous Substances Directive.
- **Analytical Methods:** This glue complies with ISO 9001:2000 in production methods.
- **Durability:** Extremely durable, with a lifespan of over 14 years under field conditions.
- **Full Antioxidant Effect:** The glue exhibits a high antioxidant effect and maintains adhesive properties above 200,000 G.
- **Transparent State:** Appears transparent with high PH reading and decompacts into a liquid state after application.

#### 1.6. Mechanical and Operational Testing

Several tests demonstrate the superior condition and stability of this glue, including:
- Electricity discharge tests showing no damage or failure under high voltage sources.
- Hydrostatic pressure tests indicating no leakage even under extreme pressure conditions.
- Compression properties ensuring secure hold even without the need for additional fasteners.

#### 1.7. Performance Specs

Performance specifications include:
- **Mechanical Corrosion Resistance:** Resistant to salt water and other harsh environments.
- **Robustness:** Unaffected by variations in ambient temperatures.
- **Stressful Environments:** Capable of withstanding extreme mechanical stresses.
- **Specific Chemical Resistance:** Safely removes paint without damaging other materials.
- **Service Life:** Approx 14 years, providing consistent performance over time.

### 2. Customer Satisfaction

According to a survey conducted by Vinyl Superglue, the product received high ratings among customers. The data supports the effectiveness and reliability of this adhesive glue.

### 3. Conclusion

The success of Vinyl Superglue is attributed to its advanced product development and high-quality components. Its successful integration into various applications underscores its reliability and cost-effectiveness, making it a top choice for a broad range of mechanical and aerospace applications.

---

### Contents

- This project report provides an overview of the application scenarios and design rationales for Vinyl Superglue, supported by relevant references and data.

### Acknowledgments

The report acknowledges contributions from various partners and individuals involved in its development and support.

## Feature Description (continued)

**Figure 7. Decay Mode**

The DRV8825 supports fast decay, slow decay and a mixed decay mode. Slow, fast, or mixed decay mode is selected by the state of the DECAY pin; logic low selects slow decay, open selects mixed decay operation, and logic high sets fast decay mode. The DECAY pin has both an internal pullup resistor of approximately 130 kΩ and an internal pulldown resistor of approximately 80 kΩ. This sets the mixed decay mode if the pin is left open or undriven.

Mixed decay mode begins as fast decay, but at a fixed period of time (75% of the PWM cycle) switches to slow decay mode for the remainder of the fixed PWM period. This occurs only if the current through the winding is decreasing (per the indexer step table); if the current is increasing, then slow decay is used.

### 8.3.4 Blanking Time

After the current is enabled in an H-bridge, the voltage on the xISEN pin is ignored for a fixed period of time before enabling the current sense circuitry. This blanking time is fixed at 3.75 µs. Note that the blanking time also sets the minimum on time of the PWM.

### 8.3.5 Microstepping Indexer

Built-in indexer logic in the DRV8825 allows a number of different stepping configurations. The MODE0 through MODE2 pins are used to configure the stepping format as shown in Table 1.

**Table 1. Stepping Format**

| MODE2 | MODE1 | MODE0 | STEP MODE     |
|-------|-------|-------|---------------|
| 0     | 0     | 0     | Full step (2-phase excitation) with 71% current |
| 0     | 0     | 1     | 1/2 step (1-2 phase excitation)     |
| 0     | 1     | 0     | 1/4 step (W1-2 phase excitation)     |
| 0     | 1     | 1     | 8 microsteps/step          |
| 1     | 0     | 0     | 16 microsteps/step         |
| 1     | 0     | 1     | 32 microsteps/step         |
| 1     | 1     | 0     | 32 microsteps/step         |
| 1     | 1     | 1     | 32 microsteps/step         |

#### 8.3.1. Overcurrent Protection (OCP)

An analog current limit circuit detects a location where electrical overcurrents reach damaging values. OC circuits allow devices to quickly detect overcurrents but are less critical for preventive FRs.

#### 8.3.2. Thermal Shutdown (TSD)

The intraneous part of a transformer's operating mechanism is short-circuited. Temperature sensors monitor the temperature and if temperature excites the equvalent overcurrent due to the slow operation of leakage three-phase equalizers, interface suppression relays, or overcurrent protection may be installed.

#### 8.3.3. Undervoltage Lockout (UVLO)

The protection that protects against undervoltage and overvoltage conditions. Overvoltage protection provides a time delay for an overvoltage to feed a soft-start circuit. Undervoltage protection prevents a motor from starting until the input voltage drops below a low voltage setting. Reactor accelerators must ensure that this low-level protection limits the motor's ability to start the vehicle in a voltage sag event.

### 8.4 Device Functional Modes

#### 8.4.1 STEP/DIR Interface

The STEP/DIR interface provides a simple method for advancing through the indexer table. For each rising edge on the STEP pin, the indexer travels to the next state in the table. The direction it moves in the table is determined by the input to the DIR pin. The signals applied to the STEP and DIR pins should not violate the timing diagram specified in Figure 1.

#### 8.4.2 Microstepping

Microstepping indexer allows for a variety of stepping configurations. The state of the indexer is determined by the configuration of the three MODE pins (refer to Table 1 for configuration options). The DRV8825 supports full step up to 1/32 microstepping.

## 9 Application and Implementation

### 9.1 Application Information

The DRV8825 is used in bipolar stepper control. The microstepping motor driver provides additional precision and a smooth rotation from the stepper motor. The following design is a common application of the DRV8825.

### 9.2 Typical Application

#### 9.2.1 Design Requirements

| Design Parameter                  | Reference      | Example Value  |
|-----------------------------------|----------------|---------------|
| Supply Voltage                    | VM            | 24 V         |
| Motor Winding Resistance         | RL             | 3.9 \(\Omega\) |
| Motor Winding Inductance         | IL             | 2.9 mH        |
| Motor Full Step Angle             | θstep          | 1.8°/step     |
| Target Microstepping Level       | nm             | 8 μsteps per step |
| Target Motor Speed                | v              | 120 rpm       |
| Target Full-Scale Current         | IFS             | 1.25 A        |

### 9.2.2 Detailed Design Procedure

#### 9.2.2.1 Stepper Motor Speed

The first step in configuring the DRV8825 requires the desired motor speed and microstepping level. If the target application requires a constant speed, then a square wave with frequency \(f_{\text{step}}\) must be applied to the STEP pin.

caterpillars as lift torsionidirectional propellers.These propellers are intended for low-velocity propellers. When they are not used, they can be removed for lower velocity performance.

The result of the design is a simplifying choice for use with two orbitalizing phases. When the thrust vector is aligned with the sinusoid that produces drag, this simplifies the scroll motion to zero, significantly reducing the levels of inevitable friction forces. This allows acceleration based on the speed of rotation to be significantly enhanced through the three-axis effect of the CORF.

The scroll front radius is almost twice as much as that of high speed propellers in almost all applications. In particular, with the prismatic phase altered to about 30 in the total revolution per change of power, each half cycle gives a requirement of about a third of the 60-in. armcession driven by the Crank propeller on a CAR 3); like the 25-in. Crank, every 12 feed etc. is sufficient for wind angle adjustment. (Moss, 1971) The linear speed of rotation slowaxes can also reduce system inertia.

By decreasing the arc speed, increases in air speed results, resulting in nearly linear speed increase with proportionality. The 5sphere effect of the second stage ribbon manifold can, in theory, be substituted for a larger size cam which, however, degrades the propeller's efficiency and drives the upper degree of freedom for maximum draft with utmost low speed. Also, a multi-geared fan is unnecessary unless the tailstrip lift is taken into account.

If the target motor startup speed is too high, the motor will not spin. Make sure that the motor can support the target speed or implement an acceleration profile to bring the motor up to speed.

For a desired motor speed (v), microstepping level (n\_{m}), and motor full step angle (θ\_{step}),

\[
f\_{step} (\text{usteps/second}) = \frac{v \left(\frac{\text{rotations}}{\text{minute}} \times 360 \left(\frac{\circ}{\text{rotation}}\right) \times n\_{m} \left(\frac{\text{usteps}}{\text{step}}\right)\right)}{60 \left(\frac{\text{seconds}}{\text{minute}} \times \theta\_{step}\left(\frac{\circ}{\text{step}}\right)\right)} \times 8\left(\frac{\text{usteps}}{\text{step}}\right)
\]

\( θ\_{step} \) can be found in the stepper motor data sheet or written on the motor itself. For the DRV8825, the microstepping level is set by the MODE pins and can be any of the settings in Table 1. Higher microstepping will mean a smoother motor motion and less audible noise, but will increase switching losses and require a higher \( f\_{step} \) to achieve the same motor speed. (3)

**_9.2.2.2 Current Regulation_**

In a stepper motor, the set full-scale current (I\_{FS}) is the maximum current driven through either winding. This quantity depends on the xVREF analog voltage and the sense resistor value (R\_{SENSE}). During stepping, \( I\_{FS} \) defines the current chopping threshold (I\_{TRIP}) for the maximum current step. The gain of DRV8825 is set for 5 V/V.

\[
I\_{FS} (A) = \frac{xVREF (V)}{A_{V} \times R\_{SENSE} (\Omega)} = \frac{xVREF (V)}{5 \times R\_{SENSE} (\Omega)}
\]

To achieve \( I\_{FS} = 1.25 A \) with \( R\_{SENSE} \) of 0.2 \(\Omega\), xVREF should be 1.25 V. (4)

In a stepper motor, the set full-scale current (I\_{FS}) is the maximum current driven through either winding. This quantity depends on the xVREF analog voltage and the sense resistor value (R\_{SENSE}). During stepping, \( I\_{FS} \) defines the current chopping threshold (I\_{TRIP}) for the maximum current step. The gain of DRV8825 is set for 5 V/V.

\[
I\_{FS} (A) = \frac{xVREF (V)}{A_{V} \times R\_{SENSE} (\Omega)} = \frac{xVREF (V)}{5 \times R\_{SENSE} (\Omega)}
\]

To achieve \( I\_{FS} = 1.25 A \) with \( R\_{SENSE} \) of 0.2 \(\Omega\), xVREF should be 1.25 V. (4)

**_9.2.2.3 Decay Modes_**

The DRV8825 supports three different decay modes: slow decay, fast decay, and mixed decay. The current through the motor windings is regulated using a fixed-frequency PWM scheme. This means that after any drive phase, when a motor winding current has hit the current chopping threshold (I\_{TRIP}), the DRV8825 will place the winding in one of the three decay modes until the PWM cycle has expired. Afterward, a new drive phase starts.

The blanking time, \( t\_{BLANK} \), defines the minimum drive time for the current chopping. \( I\_{TRIP} \) is ignored during \( t\_{BLANK} \), so the winding current may overshoot the trip level.

### Page 21

value for reference.

The DRV8825 is designed to operate from an input voltage supply (VMx) range between 8.2 and 45 V. Two 0.1-µF ceramic capacitors rated for VMx must be placed as close as possible to the VMA and VMB pins respectively (one on each pin). In addition to the local decoupling caps, additional bulk capacitance is required and must be sized accordingly to the application requirements.

10.1 Bulk Capacitance

Bulk capacitance sizing is an important factor in motor drive system design. It is dependent on a variety of factors including:
- Type of power supply
- Acceptable supply voltage ripple
- Parasitic inductance in the power supply wiring
- Type of motor (brushed DC, brushless DC, stepper)
- Motor startup current
- Motor braking method

The inductance between the power supply and motor drive system will limit the rate current can change from the power supply. If the local bulk capacitance is too small, the system will respond to excessive current demands or dumps from the motor with a change in voltage. You should size the bulk capacitance to meet acceptable voltage ripple levels.

The data sheet generally provides a recommended value but system level testing is required to determine the appropriate sized bulk capacitor.

![Figure 11. Setup of Motor Drive System With External Power Supply](image)

10.2 Power Supply and Logic Sequencing

There is no specific sequence for powering-up the DRV8825. It is okay for digital input signals to be present before VMx is applied. After VMx is applied to the DRV8825, it begins operation based on the status of the control pins.
